scenes.title: Volunteer watching Libet's revolving green cathode-ray dot to mark '-200 ms W-time' while scalp EEG rises at '-550 ms'

layout.description: High-key 1983 UCSF physiology lab with a comfortable reclining chair, vertex scalp EEG sensor lead, forearm EMG patch on the right wrist, a circular green-phosphor cathode-ray oscilloscope screen with a fast-revolving bright spot (2.56s per revolution), and a dual-channel waveform chart.

positions.who: Volunteer mannequin (in 1983 Oxford shirt with rolled right cuff)
positions.where: seated calmly watching the revolving green oscilloscope spot, flicking the right wrist briskly upward at an arbitrary moment

positions.who: Benjamin Libet (mannequin in white 1983 lab coat and glasses)
positions.where: standing beside the EEG averager pointing to the '-550 ms RP onset' rising well ahead of the '-200 ms W-mark'

props.name: revolving-spot cathode-ray oscilloscope
props.period_detail: round 1983 CRT screen numbered 5-60 around the rim with a crisp bright green spot sweeping one circle every 2.56 seconds
props.physical_behavior: lets the subject call out exact 'W-time' position (-200 ms)

props.name: forearm EMG surface electrode & vertex EEG lead
props.period_detail: clean medical surface tabs on right forearm and crown of head
props.physical_behavior: anchor 0 ms muscle firing against -550 ms cortical ramp

props.name: three-marker timeline chart (-550 ms RP -> -200 ms W -> 0 ms Muscle)
props.period_detail: large white chart plotting the rising curve with vertical markers at -550, -200, and 0 ms

actions.verb_sequence: sweeps smoothly around the circular scale -> EEG trace begins climbing at -550 ms -> Volunteer consciously notices the urge at -200 ms -> right wrist flicks cleanly upward at 0 ms
marks the 350-millisecond gap between -550 ms cortical ramp and -200 ms reported awareness

reactions.reaction: points to number '15' on the CRT rim, shocked to see the EEG line rose a third of a second earlier
highlights the remaining 150-ms 'veto' zone between -200 ms and -50 ms

scenes.wardrobe: 1983 UCSF physiology wear: white lab coat over collared shirt and tie on Libet; rolled-sleeve button shirt and chinos on volunteer.
scenes.lighting: Bright clean laboratory daylight with crisp readable oscilloscope trace.
scenes.recognition_hook: Watching a fast-sweeping oscilloscope dot at UCSF, volunteers report deciding to flick their wrist at -200 milliseconds — while scalp voltage started climbing 350 milliseconds earlier.

key_visual.description: a 1983 volunteer in a physiology chair flicking one wrist while watching a round revolving-dot oscilloscope beside a researcher pointing at a -550ms / -200ms / 0ms EEG timeline chart

scenes.title: Libet's -150 ms 'Free Won't' Veto Test

layout.description: Same oscilloscope chair where the volunteer lets an urge rise toward a preset dot mark and deliberately aborts the wrist flick at the last split-second.

positions.where: keeping right wrist completely still as the rising EEG ramp flattens back down before 0 ms

props.name: flattened veto EEG trace & flat 0-ms EMG line
props.period_detail: shows cortical build-up cancelled cleanly before any muscle fiber fires

actions.verb_sequence: feels urge at -200 ms -> applies conscious veto brake -> hand remains utterly still

reactions.reaction: points to the aborted ramp proving urges are not destiny

scenes.recognition_hook: Even in Libet's own chair, volunteers could consciously veto a rising urge 150 milliseconds before the muscle moved.

scenes.title: Schurger 2012 & Maoz 2019: Wave-averaging illusion vs real $1,000 choice

layout.description: Sunlit modern lab comparing TWO screens: random bobbing neural waves averaged at their peaks (left) vs two real $1,000 charity donation buttons where the pre-awareness RP disappears (right).

positions.where: overlaying random wave crests to show how averaging backward creates a fake 'early decision' ramp

props.name: $1,000 Charity A vs Charity B button box
props.physical_behavior: shows flat pre-decision RP during real deliberate choice

actions.verb_sequence: weighs two real charities carefully and presses button -> EEG shows deliberative prefrontal activity without a secret -550 ms autopilot boss

reactions.reaction: smiles seeing forty years of fatalism debunked

scenes.recognition_hook: Average random ocean waves backward from the biggest splash and it looks like a ramp — test real $1,000 moral choices and the 'unconscious boss' vanishes!

scenes.title: Catching a reactive impulse inside your 'Free Won't' brake window

layout.description: Bright sunlit workspace where a professional catches their thumb hovering over 'Send' on a heated message, pauses for half a second, and clicks 'Discard'.

positions.where: pausing right index finger half an inch above the desktop trackpad button before pulling back calmly

props.name: draft reply discarded cleanly
props.period_detail: screen shows calm blank compose window

actions.verb_sequence: feels reactive urge -> catches it inside the veto window -> pulls hand back

scenes.recognition_hook: You don't choose every random wave that pops into your head — you choose which ones get past your prefrontal brake.
